title: Bracket page layout
question: Kiln stays the look, scoring happens on the court, and tapping a match opens its controls. Pick how the bracket page is laid out, steer one, or re-roll.

options.label: Wall chart
options.lineage: the printed bracket poster taped to the venue wall
options.thesis: A mirrored bracket: the two halves run in from the left and right edges and meet at the final in the middle, where the champion is named.
options.viewport: Ink band with 'Bracket 1', its stage and courts; the bracket fills the width, first rounds at both edges converging on a centre final card; matches on court glow with their live score; tapping a match opens a panel with Score on Court N, court and time, hold, correct. On a phone the chart pans sideways and opens on the round being played.
options.risk: Mirroring needs width: on a phone only part of the chart shows at once. Double elimination's losers bracket runs as a second chart below.

options.label: Round by round
options.lineage: the sports app that pages through a bracket one round at a time
options.thesis: On a phone, one round fills the screen and you swipe to the next, with each match's line to its next match peeking at the edge; on desktop the whole tree shows.
options.viewport: Ink band; round tabs (Round 1 · Semis · Final) with the current round selected; that round's matches as full-width cards (teams, score chips, court or place in line), connectors to the next round peeking at the right edge; tapping a match opens its panel.
options.risk: You see one round at a time on a phone, so following a team's whole path takes swiping.

options.label: Rounds as a list
options.lineage: the order-of-play sheet read out at the scorer's table
options.thesis: On a phone the bracket reads as rounds stacked top to bottom, each match a card that names where its winner goes; on desktop the same page shows the tree.
options.viewport: Ink band; 'On court now' first (matches being played, live score chips, court); then Round 1, Semis, Final as sections, each match a card with its teams, scores, court or place in line, and 'Winner plays in Final'; tapping a match opens its panel. Desktop swaps the list for the tree with the same cards.
options.risk: On a phone the bracket's shape is described in words rather than drawn.
